A credit union and a bank are both financial institutions that provide checking and savings accounts , credit cards and other financial services, but they have some key differences in how they are run and organized.

Credit unions are member-owned. That means members have an active voice in how the credit union is run and the decisions the credit union makes. In contrast, banks are owned by their shareholders. Bank customers aren’t invited to shareholder meetings (unless they are also a shareholder), but all credit union members are regularly invited to the credit union’s annual meeting.
Another key difference is what the financial institutions do with their profits. Banks are for profit and need to pay their Board of Directors and shareholders. Since the goal is to make money, they may charge higher fees and offer lower savings rates. Credit unions, on the other hand, are not-for-profit. Any extra income they make goes back to the members in the form of better savings rates, lower loan rates, and reduced or waived fees.
Both credit unions and banks carry federal insurance for their members’ and customers’ money. Banks are insured through the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC), and credit unions are insured through the National Credit Union Administration (NCUA). The insurance limits through both agencies are the same.

United Launches New MileagePlus Debit Card (10,000 Miles Signup Bonus & More) November 4, 2025 229 Comments by Chuck Contents 1. United MileagePlus Debit Rewards Card 2. Key Details 3. Our Verdict United MileagePlus Debit Rewards Card Direct debit card link United has officially launched a new MileagePlus Debit Rewards Card, a Visa card issued by Sunrise Banks. The card earns United MileagePlus miles on debit spend and includes both spending and saving bonuses. Fees: $4 monthly fee, waived with a $2,000 average monthly balance. Welcome bonus: 10,000 MileagePlus miles after spending $500 within the first 4 months. Key Details Earning structure: 1 mile per $1 spent on United Airlines purchases, including flights and the like 1 mile per $2 spent on all other purchases Benefits: Spend bonus: 2,500 bonus miles each anniversary year after $10,000 in annual debit purchases Savings bonus: Up to 70,000 bonus miles each year based on your average account balance: $2,500 = 2,500 miles $5,000 = 5,000 miles $10,000 = 15,000 miles $25,000 = 30,000 miles $50,000 = 70,000 miles Other Notes: No credit check required Funds are FDIC insured up to $250,000 through Sunrise Banks, N.A. Our Verdict This product is mostly similar the recently-released Southwest debit card and the Wyndham debit card , and it’s as we expected . The 10,000 miles launch offer is solid for a simple debit card signup. Longer term, these debit cards will mainly appeal to debit-only users. For hobbyists this might be a way to get some rewards for certain types of purchases which don’t allow credit cards. It’s yet unknown whether someone can hold the United, Southwest, and Wyndham debit cards or if there’s some sort of limit. Also unknown what happens if you cancel these cards and eventually sign up again in terms of signup bonuses. The card adds the option of earning miles from keeping deposits in the account. At current savings APY rates , the savings bonus tiers don’t seem competitive, but maybe if the miles are non-taxable (???) then it can start making sense. Or if interest rates drop.
